questions.passage:
Rooftop Gardens

[1] In many big cities, the flat roofs of office and apartment buildings used to be nothing but bare concrete. Now more and more of them are being turned into gardens. Some grow flowers and grass, while others produce vegetables such as tomatoes, beans and lettuce.

[2] Rooftop gardens bring several benefits. Plants keep a building cooler in summer because they block strong sunlight, so less electricity is needed for air conditioning. They also absorb rainwater, which reduces the risk of flooding in the streets after heavy storms. In addition, they give birds and insects a place to live in the middle of the city.

[3] There are difficulties, too. Soil and water are heavy, so engineers must first check whether an old roof is strong enough. Building a garden on a roof can cost a lot of money, and the plants need regular care.

[4] Even so, many people think the effort is worthwhile. Office workers say they feel more relaxed after spending their lunch break among plants, and some schools use their rooftop gardens to teach children where food comes from.
questions.stem: Rooftop gardens can only grow flowers and grass.
questions.explain: 第 1 段说有的屋顶种花草，有的（others）种番茄、豆角、生菜等蔬菜，并不是“只能”种花草，所以是 False。

questions.passage:
Working From Home

[1] Not long ago, working from home was a privilege enjoyed by only a few people, such as writers and designers. Today, thanks to fast internet connections and video meetings, millions of office workers spend at least part of their week working at home.

[2] Many employees welcome the change. They no longer have to spend hours traveling to work on crowded buses or trains, and they can organize their day more freely. Parents, for example, find it easier to take their children to school and pick them up in the afternoon.

[3] However, working from home is not perfect. Some people find it hard to separate work from family life, and they end up working late into the evening. Others miss chatting with their colleagues and feel lonely.

[4] Companies have mixed feelings, too. They can save money on office space, but some managers worry that it is harder to build team spirit when people rarely meet. As a result, a growing number of companies now ask their staff to come to the office two or three days a week and work at home on the other days.
questions.stem: In the past, only a small number of people could work from home.
questions.explain: 第 1 段：不久以前，在家办公还是只有少数人（only a few people，如作家、设计师）才能享有的待遇，与题干一致，是 True。

questions.passage:
Most of us have walked into a room and then wondered why we went there. Forgetting is so common that we often see it as a weakness. Scientists, however, believe that forgetting is a normal and even useful part of how memory works.

Every day our brains receive a huge amount of information: faces, names, numbers, sounds and much more. If we remembered every detail, it would be very hard to find the information we really need. By letting unimportant details fade, the brain keeps the important ones easier to reach.

How long we remember something depends partly on how we learn it. Information that we review several times over a few days tends to stay with us much longer than information we study only once, even if we study it for a long time. Connecting new facts to things we already know also helps.

Sleep plays a part, too. Studies suggest that while we sleep, the brain reviews and organizes what we learned during the day. Students who stay up all night before an exam may therefore remember less than those who study earlier and get a good night's rest.

So the next time you forget where you put your keys, don't worry too much. Your brain may simply be doing its job.
questions.stem: According to the first paragraph, many people see forgetting as ____.
questions.explain: 第 1 段：we often see it as a weakness（我们常把它看成一种缺点）。“a useful skill”接近科学家的看法，不是多数人的看法。

lessons.title: 阅读选择：祖父的旧手表

questions.passage:
When I was twelve, my grandfather gave me an old watch for my birthday. It was not beautiful. The glass was scratched, and the leather strap was cracked. I thanked him politely, but in my heart I was disappointed. My friends had new digital watches with lights and alarms, and I wanted one too.

That evening, Grandfather sat down beside me and told me the watch's story. He had bought it with his first month's wages at the age of seventeen, when he was working in a factory far from home. For forty years it had gone with him everywhere: to his wedding, to the hospital when my mother was born, and on the long train journeys he made to visit us.

"It still keeps good time," he said, "because I have looked after it. Things last when you take care of them."

I did not really understand what he meant until many years later. When I started my first job, I found the watch at the bottom of a drawer. It had stopped. I took it to a repair shop, and after it was cleaned, it worked perfectly again. Now I wear it every day, and whenever I look at it, I think of the man who gave it to me.

questions.explain: 第 1 段：I thanked him politely, but in my heart I was disappointed——表面上礼貌道谢，心里却很失望。

lessons.title: 段落大意与补全句子：City Bicycles

questions.passage:
City Bicycles

[1] In the past twenty years, bike-sharing has spread to cities around the world. Users find a bicycle on the street, unlock it with a mobile phone app, ride it to where they want to go and leave it there for the next person.

[2] For many people, the main attraction is convenience. A shared bike is often the quickest way to cover the short distance between a subway station and an office, a trip that is too far to walk but too short for a taxi.

[3] Shared bikes are also good for the environment. Every trip made by bike instead of by car means less fuel is burned and less harmful gas goes into the air.

[4] However, the system has caused problems. In some cities, so many bikes were put on the streets that they blocked sidewalks and roads, and thousands of broken bikes ended up in piles.

[5] To solve these problems, many city governments now limit the number of bikes each company can offer and require users to park in marked areas. Some apps even charge an extra fee to people who leave a bike in the wrong place.
questions.stem: Choose the best heading for Paragraph 1 of 'City Bicycles'.
options: Too many bikes on the streets
questions.explain: 第 1 段介绍共享单车的使用过程：找车、用手机开锁、骑到目的地、留给下一个人。文中没有讲自行车的历史。

lessons.title: 段落大意与补全句子：Online Learning

questions.passage:
Online Learning

[1] Online courses were once seen as a poor substitute for "real" classes. Today they are a normal part of education for students of all ages, from schoolchildren to retired people.

[2] One reason for their popularity is flexibility. Learners can watch lectures at any time of the day, stop the video when they need to take notes, and review difficult parts as many times as they like.

[3] Online learning can also save money. Students do not have to pay for travel or accommodation, and many courses are cheaper than traditional classes. Some are even free.

[4] Yet studying alone in front of a screen requires strong self-discipline. Without a teacher watching, it is easy to put off assignments, and many learners never finish the courses they start.

[5] Experts suggest a few simple ways to succeed. Set a fixed time for study each day, find a quiet place without distractions, and join an online group so that you can discuss problems with other learners.

questions.passage:
Online Learning

[1] Online courses were once seen as a poor substitute for "real" classes. Today they are a normal part of education for students of all ages, from schoolchildren to retired people.

[2] One reason for their popularity is flexibility. Learners can watch lectures at any time of the day, stop the video when they need to take notes, and review difficult parts as many times as they like.

[3] Online learning can also save money. Students do not have to pay for travel or accommodation, and many courses are cheaper than traditional classes. Some are even free.

[4] Yet studying alone in front of a screen requires strong self-discipline. Without a teacher watching, it is easy to put off assignments, and many learners never finish the courses they start.

[5] Experts suggest a few simple ways to succeed. Set a fixed time for study each day, find a quiet place without distractions, and join an online group so that you can discuss problems with other learners.
questions.stem: Complete the sentence: Many learners never finish their online courses because ____.
options: the courses usually cost more than traditional classes
it is easy to put off work when no teacher is watching
they must pay for travel and accommodation
they are not allowed to join online groups
questions.explain: 第 4 段：Without a teacher watching, it is easy to put off assignments, and many learners never finish the courses they start。第 3 段说网课往往更便宜，也不用付交通和住宿费。

options: study only when they feel like it
watch lectures with the TV on
join an online group to discuss problems
